title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Refrigeration hack hits about 700 French supermarkets; France’s cyber agency now names Copeland as well as Danfoss
items.content_text: Attackers remotely forced supermarket refrigeration controllers into defrost on the nights of 11–13 October, pushing cabinets toward 50°C, starting fires at some stores and spoiling stock. France’s finance minister put the toll at about 700 of 10,000 supermarkets, across Intermarché, Carrefour, Monoprix, Coopérative U and E.Leclerc. CERT-FR named Danfoss AK-series controllers, then added Copeland’s Dixell XWEB systems; both vendors say most affected units are older, end-of-life models. No group, ransom demand, entry route or CVE is confirmed, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating. CERT-FR warned on 16 October that campaigns probably continue. On 19 October Claroty Team82 showed an AI agent can rebuild exploits for earlier Danfoss flaws in about 28 minutes, so operators of similar web-managed controllers should treat this as a live warning.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: AP via News4JAX (13 Oct 2026); Reuters via The Star (14 Oct 2026); Cybernews; IBTimes citing Le Monde (13 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek (15 Oct 2026) and Industrial Cyber (13 Oct 2026); Danfoss statement (12 Oct 2026); Claroty Team82 research (Aug 2026)
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Attacks on the nights of 11–13 Oct 2026; updated 16 Oct 2026 (CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 v3, 16 Oct: campaigns probably still ongoing; Reuters 13 Oct: 4,500+ Danfoss interfaces on Shodan; SecurityWeek: CERT-FR adds Copeland/Dixell; Sekoia: other EU countries; 19 Oct: Claroty Team82 AI exploit-rebuild research) — investigation ongoing

items.title: Unit 42 traces the Peerstitch implant to a FortiOS flaw used after a FortiManager compromise exposed more than 500 managed firewalls
items.content_text: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 described an intrusion at a telecommunications managed service provider in which attackers exploited FortiManager (CVE-2024-47575) to take configurations, credentials and cryptographic material for more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls. They then pushed packet-capture rules to downstream firewalls to collect HTTP, TFTP, RADIUS and LDAP traffic, and used a FortiOS auto-script path-traversal flaw (CVE-2025-61624, per the report) to load Peerstitch, a memory-resident ARM64 implant that leaves no disk binary and opens no listening port. Logs and rogue accounts were wiped. Unit 42 links some tradecraft to suspected nation-state actors; intrusions into the provider’s customer networks were not confirmed, but the stolen secrets expose them. The relayed account’s timeline is internally inconsistent, so check the original Unit 42 report for dates.
tags: Incident report — Unit 42 analysis of a telecom managed-service-provider intrusion via FortiManager and FortiOS; suspected nation-state tradecraft

items.title: Extortion group n0n claims data from 38 port, shipping and logistics firms; none has confirmed
items.content_text: SOCRadar reported on 13 October, and Industrial Cyber on 15 October, that n0n, an extortion group first seen in September 2026, listed 38 maritime and logistics organizations across 18 countries on its leak site, including container terminals, shipping lines and port IT providers; twelve are in South Korea. The group says it holds vessel schedules, container manifests, gate records and terminal-system configuration files, and reportedly seeks $2.4–14 million per victim. The group usually enters with infostealer-harvested credentials and mostly steals data rather than encrypting it. SOCRadar suggests the batch may trace to one shared application or vulnerability rather than 38 separate intrusions. Nothing is verified: no listed organization has confirmed an incident, and no control-system compromise or disruption is reported. The group’s shared 19 October publication deadline has passed; no listed organization had confirmed an incident when this edition was built.

items.title: Cyber incident disables central systems at the contractor building the Fehmarn Belt tunnel
items.content_text: Sund & Bælt, the Danish state-owned operator, said a cyber incident hit Femern Link Contractors overnight into 12 October, leaving several IT systems at the construction site affected. Local press reports that central systems were disabled. By 16 October work had partly resumed: earthworks continued, some concrete work was under way and the reinforcement-steel hall was producing, while the main production facility at Rødbyhavn was expected back “soon”. Denmark’s National Special Crime Unit is investigating. No group has claimed it, no cause has been given, and nothing published says whether industrial control systems were involved.
tags: Incident — IT systems at the Fehmarn Belt tunnel construction contractor disabled; cause and OT involvement not disclosed

items.title: A third Citrix NetScaler zero-day is exploited, and a fourth critical flaw was patched on 9 October
items.content_text: Citrix has confirmed a third NetScaler zero-day under attack, days after patching two others that were exploited for weeks before disclosure, and on 9 October it shipped a fourth fix. The exploited trio is CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88779; the federal KEV deadline for the newest passed on 7 October. The earlier pair brought web shells, rogue admin accounts and stolen configurations, and patching does not evict an intruder. The new CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS v4.0 9.5) is a SAML memory overflow that could allow code execution; no exploitation is reported, but appliances patched last week need another upgrade. Shadowserver counts more than 20,000 internet-exposed NetScaler fingerprints. Because NetScaler often fronts remote access into plant networks, an unhunted appliance is a possible foothold toward OT.
tags: Incident — three NetScaler zero-days confirmed exploited, state-sponsored actors suspected by Mandiant (not attributed); a fourth critical flaw patched 9 Oct, no exploitation reported

_otthreatfeed.category: Incident — three NetScaler zero-days confirmed exploited, state-sponsored actors suspected by Mandiant (not attributed); a fourth critical flaw patched 9 Oct, no exploitation reported

items.title: Ahold Delhaize reports a cybersecurity incident that took down Albert Heijn, Delhaize and all five US banners’ websites
items.content_text: Ahold Delhaize said a cybersecurity incident began on Sunday 11 October, and it switched off some systems as a precaution. Albert Heijn websites, apps and customer service were unavailable, online deliveries paused and loyalty systems stopped; press reports add that some electronic shelf labels showed the previous week’s promotional prices. Delhaize customers in Belgium could not place new online orders. Albert Heijn’s chief executive told broadcaster NOS that work came to a complete standstill at some distribution centres, leaving gaps on shelves; they were running again by 14 October and stores were being restocked on 16 October, while the online store stays down until next week. Cybersecurity Dive reported on 12 October that the websites of all five Ahold Delhaize USA banners (Hannaford, Stop & Shop, Giant Food, Food Lion and The Giant Company) were also down; the company has not said whether in-store operations were affected, and US store impact beyond the websites is reported but unverified. The company is investigating and putting customer, employee and partner data first; the Dutch NCSC found no link to the French refrigeration attack (Euronews, 14 October). The company says stores remain open and it has no evidence customer or associate data was stolen. No actor has been named, and nothing public links the incident to the French refrigeration attacks, so the two are treated as separate for now.

items.title: Hackers reached a US-bound tanker’s propulsion system, Bloomberg reports; the FBI says there was no disruption
items.content_text: Bloomberg reported on 2 October, citing US officials who asked not to be named, that FBI and Coast Guard investigators found hackers had temporarily accessed the propulsion system of the very large crude carrier VL Prosperity as it approached the Texas coast this summer. Neither agency has confirmed that finding on the record. The FBI’s on-record statement says there are no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental impact, and Bloomberg says it is unclear how long the access lasted or what the intruders could control. No one has been publicly blamed. VL Prosperity was boarded in the Atlantic on 21 August after it lost communications, and a second, unnamed tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico days later. On 6 October a federal official told BankInfoSecurity that both boarded tankers were reached through known, unpatched flaws in onboard systems (single unnamed-official account, not independently confirmed).
tags: Incident — Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed US officials, that hackers temporarily reached the propulsion system of the US-bound tanker VL Prosperity; FBI on record: no operational disruption, instability or crew danger; actor, duration and extent of control unknown; a second tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico

items.title: Ivanti warns attackers chained three zero-day flaws, one still unpatched, to take root on fully patched Connect Secure VPNs
items.content_text: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that a small number of customers were hit through a chain of three zero-day flaws that gave unauthenticated, root-level code execution on fully patched Connect Secure appliances. Volexity, which found it while investigating a customer incident, dates its case to 3 October (other researchers saw activity from 1 October) and tracks a previously undocumented actor, UTA0576. The intruders stole domain credentials stored on the appliance, searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, sprayed passwords and scanned internal networks, but left no web shell or backdoor. Volexity judges, with low confidence, that the group is financially motivated, and, with medium confidence, that it uses AI models for exploit development. Fixes cover two of the flaws (CVE-2026-104935); the third, a privilege-escalation bug, is still unpatched. VPN gateways like this commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary.
tags: Incident — Ivanti Connect Secure VPN zero-day chain exploited on fully patched appliances since early Oct; new actor UTA0576 tracked by Volexity; one flaw still unpatched; no OT victim named

items.title: FBI and Secret Service say the FortiBleed campaign against Fortinet VPN gateways is still running
items.content_text: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 6 October that attackers are still scanning internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways with credentials harvested earlier in the campaign. First documented in June, it had collected more than 86,000 working device credentials across 194 countries by 19 June, according to The Hacker News. No vulnerability is involved: the attackers rely on reused or leaked passwords, interception of login traffic and cracking of weakly stored hashes. Some victims were locked out when attackers created new admin accounts, then deleted or reset the legitimate ones; the FBI also says the chain has served as an entry point for ransomware affiliates, and the agencies say targets span all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors, including energy and food and agriculture. Researchers describe a Russian-speaking operator that may be selling access, with overlaps to INC and Lynx ransomware; that attribution is reported, not confirmed. Fortinet gateways often sit at the IT/OT boundary.
tags: Incident — FBI and Secret Service re-warn that the “FortiBleed” credential-harvesting campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains active; reused or leaked credentials, no CVE; no OT victim named

items.title: Claroty Team82: an AI coding agent rebuilt working exploits for Danfoss refrigeration controllers in about 28 minutes, for roughly $6
items.content_text: Team82 gave an AI coding agent only public firmware, public vulnerability identifiers and standard analysis tools, and asked it to recreate three previously disclosed Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws (CVE-2025-41450, -41451 and -41452). The agent reproduced two quickly, got the authentication bypass wrong until researchers corrected it and added a decompiler integration, and then chained the bypass with command injection to get root on a lab device. Total time was about 28 minutes and about $6 in AI usage. Team82 stresses this was not autonomous discovery: it started from known CVEs and needed human correction. Quick Censys and Shodan searches still found thousands of potentially exposed devices. Team82 links the work to the French supermarket attacks but says the real attack path is unconfirmed.
tags: Research — Claroty Team82 lab test of AI-assisted exploit development against Danfoss AK-SM 800A; builds on earlier CVEs

items.title: Palo Alto Networks patches a PAN-OS zero-day that gives root through the management interface; CISA lists it as exploited
items.content_text: Palo Alto Networks disclosed on 14 October that CVE-2026-0322 lets an attacker who already has credentials and network reach to the PAN-OS management interface run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama appliances. The company reports very limited exploitation and published three attacker IP addresses; Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected. Fixes cover PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2, with the 11.2.16 build due on 15 October, and there is no workaround beyond limiting management access to trusted internal addresses. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a federal deadline of 17 October. Firewalls like these often sit on the IT/OT boundary, so a management interface reachable from corporate networks or the internet is the exposure to remove. BleepingComputer did not get answers on who is behind the attacks or whether intruders moved further inside.
tags: Advisory — Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS management-interface remote code execution (CVE-2026-0322, CVSS 8.6), exploited in “very limited” attacks; added to CISA KEV

items.title: CISA flags six vulnerabilities in the Eclipse Milo OPC UA library used across energy, water, chemical and manufacturing
items.content_text: CISA published advisory ICSA-26-288-01 on 15 October covering six flaws in Eclipse Milo, an open-source Java OPC UA client and server stack that vendors embed in industrial gateways, historians and SCADA software. The worst, CVE-2026-60007, is a padding-oracle weakness in username-token handling rated 9.1 under CVSS v4.0; the others score between 6.9 and 8.8. Versions up to 1.1.4 are affected, and the fix is Milo 1.1.5 or later. CISA reports no known exploitation. Because the library is bundled inside other products, owners may not know they run it, so the practical work is asking vendors whether their OPC UA components use Milo. The advisory header says five flaws but lists six CVEs.
tags: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-288-01: six flaws in the open-source Eclipse Milo OPC UA stack; no exploitation reported

items.title: Siemens, Rockwell and ABB release October fixes: critical flaws in S7-1500 CPUs, Industrial Edge and ArmorBlock
items.content_text: SecurityWeek’s 14 October roundup says Siemens published 17 advisories. Three are rated critical: certain Simatic S7-1500 CPUs (which inherit hundreds of flaws in an embedded Linux subsystem), Industrial Edge devices, and the Ruggedcom Crossbow Station Access Controller; several others are high, covering Simatic IPC, WinCC, Desigo and more. Rockwell fixed two flaws in the 1732E ArmorBlock I/O module, including a critical one that lets an unauthenticated attacker change the web-server password and take over the admin account. Schneider listed high-severity issues in Pro-face/Harmony HMIs and Sage RTUs. ABB disclosed a dynovaPRO password-reset flaw and said logs show 26 password changes across 9 customers that could be testing; it knows of no exploitation. We could not verify CVE IDs or scores, so none are given.
tags: Advisory — October ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens (17 advisories), Rockwell 1732E ArmorBlock, Schneider Electric, ABB dynovaPRO; no exploitation reported; CVE/CVSS not verified

items.title: Siemens Software Center flaw is being abused to side-load malware in ClickFix attacks
items.content_text: Siemens fixed CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS v4 8.4), a DLL search-path weakness in Siemens Software Center, the installer and update tool many engineering workstations carry. Attackers paired a genuine, validly signed copy of the program with malicious DLLs and used ClickFix lures, which trick users into running commands themselves, to infect Windows PCs. Siemens ties the activity to the Romulus ClickFix campaign, which Forescout has linked to the LegionLoader malware; the operators are unknown. Siemens says none of its systems or update channels were breached and the malicious packages did not come from them. Huntress reported the flaw. Version 4.0.9.8 fixes it, and installed copies update on next launch.
tags: Advisory — Siemens Software Center DLL side-loading flaw (SSA-580366), abused in ClickFix malware campaigns against Windows PCs; engineering-workstation relevance, no OT process impact reported

items.title: BeyondTrust patches a Remote Support zero-day exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus espionage actor
items.content_text: BeyondTrust has fixed CVE-2026-102764, an authentication bypass in self-hosted Remote Support appliances (version 26.2.3 and earlier) that lets an unprivileged remote attacker perform file operations. Mandiant and Google’s threat-intelligence group link the exploitation to a suspected state-sponsored espionage actor they track as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221); CrowdStrike calls it Warp Panda. After getting in, the intruders used web shells, escalated to root, wiped logs and harvested stored credentials for lateral movement. SaaS customers were patched on 8 October; self-hosted customers must patch themselves. Shadowserver counts more than 1,400 exposed instances, and Google expects opportunistic exploitation to follow. No victims are named, and none is reported in critical infrastructure. Integrators and OEMs often use this class of tool for vendor access to plants, so its owners should check it. We did not find a CVSS score, so none is given.
tags: Advisory — BeyondTrust Remote Support authentication-bypass zero-day (BT26-05), exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor; vendor remote-access tooling often used to reach plant systems; no OT victims named

items.title: CISA flags a critical remote-code-execution flaw in Grid Protection Alliance’s openPDC and openHistorian grid-data software
items.content_text: On 8 October CISA published ICSA-26-281-02, covering several classes of high-severity vulnerabilities in the Grid Protection Alliance’s openPDC and openHistorian, open-source software that utilities use to collect and store time-series grid measurements (our description; CISA lists the energy sector). The most serious, CVE-2026-100730, is a deserialization flaw that can give an unauthenticated network attacker remote code execution, which CISA scores CVSS v3.1 9.8; fixes are in openPDC 2.9.482 and openHistorian 2.8.585. CISA reports no known public exploitation. The relevance for OT teams is that these servers sit between substation or phasor data sources and control-center analytics, so a flaw there is a possible stepping stone between networks rather than a direct control-loop risk. Affected versions and fixes are listed in the advisory and are not repeated here.
tags: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-281-02, Grid Protection Alliance openPDC and openHistorian (energy-sector grid data software); CVSS v3 9.8 as reported; no known exploitation

items.title: Two threat-intel firms report exploitation attempts against SonicWall’s maximum-severity SMA1000 flaw, days after hotfixes shipped
items.content_text: Previdian and Defused both report their honeypots receiving requests consistent with CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS 10), a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the SMA1000 WorkPlace interface that SonicWall patched on 6 October; Defused dates its first hits to 8 October (SecurityWeek, 12 October). Neither has determined whether any attempt succeeded, and SonicWall’s advisory did not flag active exploitation. Fixed builds are 12.5.0-03082 and 12.4.3-03670. The flaw is reachable remotely without authentication on SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v models; SMA100 and firewall SSL-VPN are not affected. Shadowserver counts more than 400 exposed SMA1000 appliances. The same interface was hit by SSRF flaws in July and September that were exploited, so quick scanning after a patch is plausible. These gateways often give vendors and integrators a path toward plant networks.
tags: Advisory — SonicWall rates CVE-2026-102255, an SSRF in the SMA1000 Appliance WorkPlace interface, as maximum severity; unauthenticated and remote; two threat-intel firms report exploitation attempts (not confirmed successful); not in CISA KEV as of 12 Oct

items.title: FERC staff publish CIP audit lessons: unregistered new generation, stacked low-impact systems and AI tools in CIP networks
items.content_text: On 13 October FERC released a staff report drawing on its fiscal-2026 audits of NERC-registered entities. Most cybersecurity processes reviewed met the mandatory CIP standards, but auditors found three recurring problems. Some generator owners registered new resources late or never identified their BES Cyber Systems, and several inverter-based resources were running commercially without the required cyber evaluation, one more than a year past the threshold. Two entities treated systems as low impact that together met the medium-impact criteria once affiliate and contractor control was counted. Auditors also saw what the report calls “super intelligence” (SI) tools — chatbots, assistants and automated analytics — appearing inside CIP-networked environments, where they can mimic user behavior and open unauthorized access or lateral-movement paths faster than compliance programs adapt. The report is staff guidance, not a new requirement, and it suggests NERC may consider further guidance or standards changes.
tags: Regulation — FERC staff report on CIP audit lessons learned flags late registration of new generation, aggregated low-impact systems and AI tools inside CIP networks; no CVE
